props.heading: A headless CMS in one small Go binary
props.subheading: Describe your content in YAML. Hydrogen gives you an admin with live visual editing and APIs that any website or app can read. Add a SQLite file or Postgres, and that is the whole stack.

props.caption: From nothing to a running admin
props.code:
go install github.com/hydrogencms/hydrogen/cmd/hydrogen@latest
hydrogen new -module example.com/mysite mysite && cd mysite
hydrogen migrate
echo "a long passphrase" | hydrogen users:create-admin admin
hydrogen dev        # http://localhost:8080/admin/

props.heading: What every project gets
props.intro: The core covers what every project needs. Everything else is a module you add with one command.

props.text: Every write is validated against your YAML schema, and Hydrogen generates typed Go and TypeScript, an OpenAPI document and, if you want one, a GraphQL schema.
props.title: Typed from the schema

props.text: Editors build pages from typed blocks in a live preview of your real frontend, with outlines, drag and drop and inline text editing. Several editors can work on one page together.
props.title: Live visual editing

props.text: Each consumer, a website in one language or a mobile app, is a channel in config with its own languages, fallbacks, collections and access.
props.title: Channels

props.text: Drafts and versions, a trash, scheduled releases, reviews, share links for previews, and locale overlays for markets.
props.title: Editorial workflow

props.text: Roles, policies and limitations, API tokens, rules in code and an audit log. AI agents use the same tokens, validation and review as people.
props.title: Access control

props.text: Typed hooks, endpoints, jobs and commands in your project, WebAssembly hooks in any language, and admin extensions as custom elements.
props.title: Customisable in Go

content.text: Every commit to Hydrogen runs the same budget checks: a new project builds to a binary under 25 MB, starts in under 200 ms and idles in under 40 MB of memory, or the build fails.
